case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Deseret News Publishing Co. v. Salt Lake County
key_cases.holding: The Court held that government records are presumptively public under GRAMA and that the governmental entity bears the burden of justifying a nonpublic classification; it ordered release of an internal investigative report because the public interest in governmental accountability outweighed the asserted privacy intrusion.
key_cases.relevance: It makes internal investigative reports — the raw material of oversight — presumptively obtainable.
key_cases.quote: government records are presumptively public under GRAMA, and thus, the County bears the burden of proving that it properly classified the investigative report as nonpublic

key_cases.case_name: Schroeder v. Utah Attorney General's Office
key_cases.holding: The Court held that records lawfully obtained by warrant or subpoena are not exempt from GRAMA on search-and-seizure grounds, that two documents were properly classified as attorney work product, but that disclosure was nonetheless required because the closed investigation weakened the interests favoring protection.
key_cases.relevance: It supports outside oversight by making closed-investigation records obtainable when the public interest in accountability predominates.
key_cases.quote: we ultimately reverse the district court's ruling because the State terminated its investigation years ago, so the interests favoring protection are not as compelling as those favoring disclosure

key_cases.case_name: J.J.W. v. State, Division of Child & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that the Juvenile Expungement Statute gives the juvenile court broad authority to order DCFS to expunge its records, including entries in the non-public child abuse Database, but reversed the particular order because DCFS had no notice or opportunity to be heard.
key_cases.relevance: It delineates the limited access rules that oversight bodies must work within when seeking DCFS records.
key_cases.quote: the plain language of section 78-82-905 grants the juvenile court broad authority to expunge records

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Utah Code § 80-2-602(1)

Exception: a member of the clergy, as to a confession made directly by the perpetrator while the clergy member is functioning in a ministerial capacity and without the confessor's consent, and only if canon law or church doctrine or practice binds the clergy member to maintain the confidentiality of the confession; the clergy member must still report abuse or neglect learned from any source other than that confession — Utah Code § 80-2-602(3)(a), (4)(a)

Exception: an attorney, or an individual employed by the attorney, where the knowledge arises from representing a client, unless the attorney is permitted to reveal it to prevent reasonably certain death or substantial bodily harm — Utah Code § 80-2-602(3)(b)

other: A child at risk of being neglected or abused because another child in the same home is neglected or abused; Dealing in material harmful to a child; That a child's natural parent: (1) intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causes the death of another parent of the child, (2) is identified by a law enforcement agency as the primary suspect in an investigation for intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causing the death of another parent of the child, or (3) is being prosecuted for or has been convicted of intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causing the death of another parent of the child
